title: Lightweight trace contracts for multi-hop session handoff
content:
Purpose
This doc outlines a minimal, low-cost tracing contract for multi-hop conversational/session flows that cross service/process boundaries (API gateway -> routing -> model-serving -> postprocess). The goal is to provide just enough provenance to: 1) reconstruct user-visible sessions, 2) attribute latency to hop boundaries, and 3) enable targeted drilldowns from compact dashboards without incurring trace storage explosion.

Background and motivation
- Our inference stacks often fan out (embedding lookup, reranker, multi-model fanout). Full-fidelity tracing for every token and subcall is expensive in storage and query time.
- Operators need quick answers: Which hop is adding 90th percentile latency? Is cold KV cache the culprit? Are falls back to a cheaper model increasing downstream variance?
- We need a lightweight contract that teams can implement quickly and that meshes with adaptive sampling and dashboard widgets.

Assumptions and constraints
- Multi-tenant but traces must avoid PII/PHI. Redaction rules apply.
- Sampling budget is limited: default 1% reservoir global, plus signal-driven bumping (canary, error spike, low-slo cohort).
- Instrumentation should be language-agnostic (HTTP headers / tracectx) and not require heavy SDKs for sidecars.
- Minimal overhead: aim for <200 bytes additional metadata per request in headers.

Trace contract (minimal fields) - required for every hop
1) session_id (string): stable per logical user session/interaction. If unavailable at generation point, populate with derived id (sha256(prefix + ephemeral_id)) and mark as derived via attribute session_id_derived=true.
2) trace_id (string): standard parent trace id for distributed tracing.
3) span_id (string): hop-local span id.
4) hop_role (enum): one of [edge, router, model_inference, postprocess, cache, storage].
5) hop_latency_ms (int): measured duration for the hop (ms).
6) kv_warm (bool, optional): if hop accesses KV for prefix/kv cache; true/false/unknown.
7) model_variant (string, optional): short id for model variant e.g., m-7b-q4f.
8) sample_reason (enum): one of [default, error, canary, manual, high_latency, low_slo_customer].
9) tenant_id (string, optional): tenant for multi-tenant attribution (hashed at source if sensitive).
10) trace_version (string): contract version, e.g., v1.0.

Recommended spans and attributes (nice-to-have)
- token_count (int) for inference spans (approx tokens produced)
- batch_size (int) at entry to serving runtime
- route_decision (string) when smart routing picked a variant e.g., fallback->cheap_q4
- cpu_ms / gpu_ms (int) when available from runtime metrics
- error_code / error_message (string) short-cased; full message goes to secure logs only

Sampling and retention strategy
- Global reservoir: 1% of all traces retained for 30d.
- Error-focused sampling: retain 100% traces for spans with error_code present for 90d.
- Canary/experimental routes: 100% retention for flagged model_variant or route_decision values for 14d.
- Session-based escalation: if a given session_id produces >3 high-latency events in 10 minutes, increase sampling of that session to 10% for 1h.

Dashboard mapping and widget prioritization
- Tile naming convention: <tier> / <scope> / <metric> (e.g., ops/edge/latency-p95). Use scope labels to indicate trace linkage: session, tenant, model_variant.
- Lightweight drill path: dashboard tile -> top-10 trace summaries -> selected trace opens span waterfall. Summaries derive from contract fields only (no full-span dump).
- Widget prioritization rules (order of placement): 1) SLO-critical latency panels (p50/p95/p99) by hop_role, 2) error-rate and error-type heatmap, 3) KV-warmth and cold-start probes, 4) model-fallback ratio and cost delta, 5) tracing-coverage panel (sample_rate by route).
- Cost-aware widget culling: any widget that needs full-span queries triggers audit tag; default retention for such widgets is reduced to 7d unless owner appeals.

Operator play: investigation quick steps
1) From latency alert, open tile -> check hop_role heatmap. If hop shows high p95: toggle to sample_reason=high_latency to list recent traces.
2) If kv_warm=false spikes, check backend cache eviction panels and recent deployment events.
3) For multi-model fanout, compare model_variant slices and inspect route_decision for fallbacks.
4) Mark suspicious traces with investigation_ticket id; this raises trace retention for that session for 72h.

Implementation guidance for services
- Libraries: provide a tiny header helper that accepts session_id, hop_role, model_variant, kv_warm, and populates trace_version and sample_reason. Keep header <= 256 bytes.
- For services without SDKs, document curl/edge examples.
- Redaction: tenant_id must be hashed using salt per deployment; do not include raw prompts or outputs in spans. For debugging, move full payloads into secure logs with link reference id only in spans.

Migration and rollout checklist
- Phase 0 (week 0–2): publish contract, add header helper, update edge and router to emit minimal fields.
- Phase 1 (week 2–5): add hop_latency_ms instrumentation in model-serving and postprocess; enable sample_reason high_latency bump.
- Phase 2 (week 6–8): dashboard templates and drill path implementation; operators test runbook.
- Phase 3 (week 9–12): enable adaptive session escalation, refine sampling budgets, shrink verbose traces.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- session_id derivation: how to best correlate anonymous browser sessions vs. API tokens without leaking identity? Proposal: prefer client-provided session_id; otherwise derive from request fingerprint and record session_id_derived=true.
- retention cost cap: what is the hard budget for trace storage? Need finance input (ask FinOps).
- SDK adoption: do we force minor SDK changes at runtime services or accept best-effort headers?

Action items
- Aisha: finalize header helper repo + tiny README (due 2025-02-07).
- Ravi: prototype dashboard drill path and sample_reason filter (due 2025-02-21).
- Samantha: run a 2-week canary with full retention on a low-volume route (due 2025-02-28).
- Diego: cost estimation with FinOps for expected retention tiers (due 2025-02-14).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally minimal: design tradeoffs prioritize fast triage over exhaustive full-span capture. We expect to iterate after initial canary. Please comment where fields feel insufficient for debugging and call out any downstream query cost estimates.

References
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/trace-contracts-draft
- Example header helper: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/tree/main/header-helper
- Related ticket: ENG-1428
